The function $f(x)$ is defined and differentiable on $[1,5].$ The graph of ${f}^{′}(x),$ the derivative of $f(x),$ is shown above, where the area of the region between the graph and the $x$-axis is $2\pi .$ Find the maximum value of $f(x)$ on the interval $[1,5]$ given that $f(1)=-3\pi .$

question.worked_solution:
According to the candidate test, the maximum value of $f(x)$ on $[1,5]$ must occur at a critical point or an endpoint of the interval. 

**Step 1**: Find the critical points:

We see that ${f}^{′}(x)$ is defined everywhere on $x\in (1,5),$ and ${f}^{′}(x)\ne 0$ on this interval. Therefore, the candidates are $x=1,5.$

**Step 2**: Compute the value of $f$ for each candidate using the fundamental theorem of calculus:

Using the given information and the fundamental theorem of calculus, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1) & =-3\pi  \\ f(5) & =f(1)+{\int }_{1}^{5}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-3\pi -2\pi  \\  & =-5\pi \end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Select the largest value of $f$ from our candidates. 

Comparing the values of $f$ found in step $2,$ we have

$$
{f}_{\text{max}}=max\{-3\pi ,-5\pi \}=-3\pi .
$$

Therefore, the maximum value of $f$ is ${f}_{\text{max}}=-3\pi ,$ and the value of $x$ that maximizes $f(x)$ is ${x}_{\text{max}}=1.$
